checked.target: src/sim/pickups.ts beginPickupTick / collectPickups (ties, respawn, boost timing)
checked.how: Traced tick by tick. Fire tick sets boostTicks 90 and boosts 90 ticks (90..1, then 0). A box taken at the end of tick T is absent in views T..T+299 and present at T+300. Cars are visited in index order, so the lowest index takes a contested box and a later car takes the next present box in reach. `break` stops a car taking two. Armed cars are skipped.

beginPickupTick runs before stepCars and collectPickups after, as on main. The countdown returns early, so nothing changes before GO. Raw `inputs[k].action` is read; a decoded replay's non-enumerable `action` still reads true. Per-car arrays are built fresh per world, so nothing leaks across races. Tracks without pickups have no state and no armed/boostTicks keys.

checked.target: src/sim/car.ts stepCars signature (boosted: number → readonly boolean[])
checked.how: Grepped every stepCars/beginPickupTick/collectPickups/createPickups caller in src, tests, harness, guardrails and spikes. Only world.ts and tests that pass three arguments remain. Nothing still passes a car index. Typecheck passes (gates.md).

checked.target: src/sim/bot.ts target/limit rewrite (car 0 and tracks without pickups unchanged)
checked.how: pace*min(25,x) equals min(pace*25,pace*x) bit for bit (rounding is monotone), so `target` matches main. Without world.pickups, `p` is undefined, boosting is false and there is no action key. For car 0, the carIndex>0 guards keep want=target and fireOk is all zeros. This matches G2 at +0.0% for Bramble Bends and Hay Loop.

Traced the window. The initial count covers d=0..span, then each step adds blocked[(i+span+1)%n] and removes blocked[i], which gives exactly [i, i+span], including wrap-around and a window longer than the lap. Ramp samples use the same lip=floor(at*n) as noPass. pos.seg is always in [0,count) (track.ts projectOnSegment).

checked.target: bot firing guards and braking while boosting
checked.how: Fire needs armed, fireOk[pos.seg], dirt and not airborne; the reverse branch returns before it. want=min(limit,32) is at least target, so the brake rule is unchanged. At limit+2 the lateral acceleration is about 23, under grip 24. FIRE_CLEAR is 64.8 units against at most 48 boosted plus about 4 braking, so the boost ends well before any blocked sample or ramp.

checked.target: Dust Bowl fire zone vs the second box row (re-arm during or just after a boost)
checked.how: From the centreline I estimate curvature above the bots' 0.032 threshold only near the two end-curve apexes, plus the ramp at s≈31–36. That leaves a clear zone of roughly s≈143–240, and the second row at s≈187 lies inside it. A bot can take a box just after a boost and fire again. That is the player's rule too (spec: 'same rules'), and AC2/AC5 hold on the tested seeds, so I did not report it.

checked.target: G2 teleport limit (0.625) with boosting bots
checked.how: A boosted free step is 0.533. Push-outs against the motion shorten steps, and forward pushes need closing speeds that bots at ≤32 don't have. tests/sim/bot.test.ts asserts maxStep < limit for two-bot Dust Bowl on 5 seeds, and G2 reports worst step 0.515. I found no concrete over-limit trace, so I did not report it.

checked.target: src/game.ts tick/startRace/setPaused, src/ui/race-ui.ts sync, src/render/scene.ts update
checked.how: Bots are built per startRace from the new world, and each bot.input is called once per tick. Pause stops the loop, so bots and pickup state freeze. race-ui reads only racers[0].armed and whether view.pickups exists. scene.update shows or hides boxes from view.pickups on every draw, so AI-taken boxes vanish like the player's. The diff adds no listeners or timers.

encodeInputs sets bit 2 for any car's action, and decodeInputs restores `action` for any car. runReplay goes through stepWorld, so AI fires replay identically. The test round-trips the JSON envelope and re-runs live bots against the recorded player inputs, comparing every tick's RaceView.

No Math.random, Date, performance, window or document in src/sim. The diff has no @ts-ignore, eslint-disable, .skip/.only/.todo/it.fails, env sniffing or reviewer-directed text. Module scratch (clean, start, nearby, bodyTs) is rewritten every tick, so worlds don't influence each other. Bot RNG draws are unchanged.

Grepped the tree (minus journal) for 'AI cars never', 'only the player', 'car 0 only' and similar. The only player-only pickup wording was in types.ts, pickups.ts, world.ts, the car.ts stepCars doc and the bot.ts header, and the diff fixes all of them.

AC1–AC8 each have an `AC<n>:` test in a new file. Each fails on main, because bots never arm or fire there. vitest include is tests/**/*.test.ts, so the helper isn't run as a suite. I traced the AC3 window comparison, AC4 (car 0 reverses while holding, then steers to the absent box) and the AC7 per-arming predicate. No existing test is edited.

G1 821/821 (main 813, +8 matches the 8 new tests). G2 shows Bramble Bends and Hay Loop at +0.0% and Dust Bowl at -2.3%, the intended change. G3 replays are recorded on the frozen dust-bowl-classic track (record-replays.ts header), which has no pickups. G8 is clean.

checked.target: Edge cases: carCount 1, empty pickups, short inputs, aliasing
checked.how: carCount 1 gives length-1 arrays and no bots. An empty pickups list gives an undefined state. Inputs shorter than the cars read `?.action` as undefined. beginPickupTick returns the live `boosting` array, but stepCars only reads it synchronously. No code adds cars to a world after creation (grep).

A car with finishTick set keeps driving (bots) or coasting (player) and still collects and fires. The spec says every car follows the same rules, and the player's finished car does the same, so I treated it as design rather than a bug.

Its hunk context still shows `stepCars(world.cars, clean, world.track);` from before B12, so it was already stale on main. It is a protected file and not part of tonight's diff, so I did not report it.
